basis: Chronic cervicofacial infection directly involves subcutaneous tissues with infiltrative abscesses and sinus tracts; an oral portal alone does not establish gastrointestinal disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: oral commensal origin and entry through dental tissues do not establish common direct gastrointestinal involvement.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infiltrative infection of cervicofacial subcutaneous tissues with abscesses and draining sinuses defines the usual disease.

basis: Uterine duplication and obstructed hemivagina affect reproductive organs; the supplied concept does not establish renal agenesis or its frequency.

decisions.renal: none: associated renal agenesis cannot be assumed to define this uterovaginal malformation; the supplied evidence establishes no renal abnormality.

basis: Lysosomal storage with defining skeletal and joint disease; myopia occurs in 3/3. Functionally significant cardiac involvement is not established in >=30%; retinitis pigmentosa is rare.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac complications are rarely clinically significant ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK24701/)); common valve thickening alone is insufficient.

basis: Immune-mediated granulomatous arthritis and uveitis define disease; granulomatous dermatitis occurs in 42/44 (~95%). The three-primary cap places skin involvement in the involved tier.

decisions.ocular: primary: granulomatous uveitis is a defining diagnostic feature, present in 39/54 (~72%), with potential permanent visual damage.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: granulomatous dermatitis occurs in 42/44 (~95%); the primary cap reserves three positions for immune mechanism, arthritis and uveitis.

basis: MELAS defines mitochondrial metabolic encephalomyopathy; sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 40-70% across MELAS. MTTH-specific frequency remains uncertain.

decisions.otologic: involved: intrinsic sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 40-70% in MELAS; parent-disease frequency is used because MTTH-specific estimates are unavailable.

basis: Motor-neuron degeneration defines disease; contractures and scoliosis in 2/3 and muscle atrophy in 1/3 follow denervation and spasticity rather than direct muscle or joint disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures/scoliosis (2/3) and atrophy (1/3) are consequences of denervation and spasticity; they do not establish direct myopathy or arthropathy.

basis: Definition covers intestinal protein loss across causes. CHAPLE-associated immunoglobulin depletion (11/11) does not establish common immunodeficiency across this broader concept.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: the broad definition describes immune depletion in severe cases; CHAPLE-specific frequencies cannot establish >=30% immune dysfunction across all protein-losing enteropathies.

basis: Defining eye/pituitary defects; developmental delay and auditory canal atresia each 80-99%. Limb anomalies omitted at the four-axis cap; individual digit defects and renal hypoplasia are <30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: defining limb abnormalities qualify but are omitted at the four-axis cap, prioritizing severe eye/pituitary defects and frequent CNS and auditory canal abnormalities.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia is a direct structural ear abnormality reported in 80-99%; occasional hearing impairment does not negate that lesion.

basis: Radial/thumb aplasia 3/3; renal agenesis and esophageal atresia/TEF each 2/3. Hydrocephalus 2/3 and ear malformations 1/3 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: absent radii and thumbs occur in 3/3, establishing common structural skeletal involvement; the defining Fanconi blood/marrow disorder remains primary.

basis: Defined by severe, intractable vomiting with dehydration, weight loss and electrolyte derangement; digestive dysfunction and metabolic disturbance have axes despite the obstetric setting.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe intractable vomiting defines pathological digestive dysfunction; primary classification does not require structural gastrointestinal injury.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: electrolyte imbalance and dehydration are explicit defining manifestations; electrolyte disorders fall within this axis.
